reader.notes: GenerateCore presents the RH only in its !_started branch, which Initiate resets and TerminateCore never enters when no GENERATE ran; GenerateSummary takes the same path. Classes a, e and f do not apply: the rule has no variable-length, file-organization or numeric operand, and a report file is sequential only.

refuter.evidence: Probes run with run_probe.py --std 85 under refute-1985-149/runs. rtype1-001: RH1 LINE 1 NEXT GROUP PLUS 1 printed on L1, U-RH1 ran first (LC=0), and PH (LINE PLUS 1) followed on L3. rtype2-003: RH1 NEXT GROUP 2 (absolute) printed first, U-RH1 before every other USE, PH LINE 3 on L3, and the first GENERATE was a nonprintable detail D0. rtype1 R3: RH NEXT GROUP NEXT PAGE stood alone on page 1. rtype2/rreinit-001: after TERMINATE, a re-INITIATE plus GENERATE processed the RH again, once. rnodet-002: a report with no RH and no detail took GENERATE report-name. Class c: ron-001 and rfor-001 (the 2002 ON/FOR word before a TYPE CH/CF operand) gave COBOL0900 at 85, and rok-001 (TYPE CH FINAL) compiled. cite: OK §1985:XIII.3.20.4 GR2 'processed during the execution of the chronologically first GENERATE statement for that report'; OK §1985:XIII.3.10.6 GR5a 'places the NEXT GROUP integer into LINE-COUNTER'. Side observation, not this rule: after a re-INITIATE the second instance's RH (LINE 1) lands on the next physical line (line 8 of an 8-line page, rreinit-001) with no page eject, and --std 2023 (rreinit-002) does the same. That is a presentation-position question under §1985:XIII.3.10.6 GR3a (OK 'presented on the line number specified by the integer of its LINE NUMBER clause'), downstream of the landed PB1667 arm 2.
